title: Review of c42's more-seeds finding on seed 5 (128^2) with its predator-free twin: predators divide (36 persistent splits, generation 3) and coexist with prey to t=12000; prey divide weakly (3 persistent splits, generation 1), like the finding's seed 3; the twin is a frozen emulsion of 77
summary: Labkit re-run of the claim's world.py unchanged, seed 5, 128^2, 120 frames, --lineage-k 5 (rerun/seed5), and the predator-free twin pred_on 0 on the same seed (twin/seed5). With predators: 29 predators and 4 prey at t=12000 (prey 5-15 through the run), predator persistent splits 36 (generation 3, merge/split 0.45), prey persistent splits 3 (generation 1); the claim's splits2.py finds 3 prey divisions after t=2000. Twin: 77 static prey, 12 persistent splits, 1 prey division after t=2000 by splits2.py.

observations.D: rerun/seed5/FACTS.md: predator persistent splits 36, generation 3, predators present at the end (29); prey 3 persistent splits, generation 1; twin/seed5: 77 frozen prey, 1 late division (splits2.py) vs 3 with predators

controls_run.D: twin/seed5 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration, window)

verdicts.limitation: On seed 5 the prey reach only generation 1 (3 persistent splits), as on the finding's seed 3, so prey generation >= 2 now holds on 4 of 6 seeds; predator division replicates on every seed. 128^2 only, one fresh seed.
